title: Analytes and specimen types
summary: Maintain named catalog items and the versioned validity policies attached to specimen types.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Analytes lists the substances and validity markers methods measure. Search by code, name or LOINC, then open a row to inspect its supplied identifiers. Add analyte records a new catalog item.

Specimen types lists the types used during receipt and their validity-policy version states. Open a type to inspect its policy versions, categories, actions and qualifier text. A new policy draft follows the available review and approval actions.

sections.title: Good practice
paragraphs: Use codes and names provided by the laboratory’s configuration owner. Confirm analyte identity before assigning external codes or drug classes; do not infer them from a similar name.

Validity categories and their consequences are laboratory decisions. Enter only the approved categories and wording. A missing policy or identifier should remain visible as a configuration issue until the responsible person supplies it.

sections.title: If you cannot continue
paragraphs: Check whether you are viewing a draft or a version in effect. Unapproved policy content is not made active simply by saving it. If a receiving or review workflow lacks the expected type or category, ask the configuration owner to review the relevant record and version.

pages.title: Analytes
pages.purpose: Register the drugs and specimen-validity markers referenced by analytical methods.
pages.access: View with the configuration access offered to your account. Adding and drafting require Manage configuration; approval and retirement require Approve configuration. The engine checks authority again when saving.

fields.name: Find analytes
fields.meaning: Locate an existing analyte before adding another.
fields.values: Code, name or LOINC text; blank shows all.

fields.name: Code
fields.meaning: Stable laboratory identifier used to recognize and reference the record.
fields.values: Laboratory-assigned letters, digits, period, underscore or hyphen.
fields.rules: Required; at most 64 characters; unique for this record type. Choose carefully: this screen does not rename codes.

fields.name: Name
fields.meaning: Human-readable label staff see when selecting the record.
fields.rules: Required; up to 200 characters; surrounding spaces are removed and control characters are refused.

fields.name: LOINC code / LOINC
fields.meaning: External observation identifier supplied for this analyte.
fields.rules: Optional; up to 64 characters using letters, digits, period, underscore or hyphen. It is retained as supplied; saving does not prove that the mapping is clinically appropriate.

fields.name: Drug class code / Drug class
fields.rules: Optional; same code syntax and length limit. Do not infer a class from the analyte name; missing values show Not provided.

actions.name: Add analyte
actions.does: Save a new analyte and open its details.
actions.availableWhen: Manage configuration; a new unique code and name are provided.
actions.result: The analyte becomes available to method drafts.

actions.name: Open row / Previous / Next / Close
actions.does: Inspect saved identifiers and move through the filtered list.
actions.result: Read-only details open; this screen has no rename or delete action.

restrictions: A registered analyte is not an approved assay or interpretation rule.
workflow: Search by code, name and any known LOINC mapping.
Enter the authorized code and name plus supplied external identifiers.
Save and inspect the resulting record before using it in a method.

troubleshooting.recovery: Open and check the existing record. Do not create a slightly altered duplicate to bypass the conflict.

pages.title: Specimen types
pages.purpose: Find registered specimen types and open their version history, or add a new record.
pages.access: View with the configuration access offered to your account. Adding and drafting require Manage configuration; approval and retirement require Approve configuration. The engine checks authority again when saving.

fields.name: Find specimen types
fields.meaning: Narrow the displayed directory without changing saved records.
fields.values: Any part of the code or name; blank shows all.
fields.rules: Optional; matching is on the loaded directory.

fields.name: Code
fields.meaning: Stable laboratory identifier used to recognize and reference the record.
fields.values: Laboratory-assigned letters, digits, period, underscore or hyphen.
fields.rules: Required; at most 64 characters; unique for this record type. Choose carefully: this screen does not rename codes.

fields.name: Name
fields.meaning: Human-readable label staff see when selecting the record.
fields.rules: Required; up to 200 characters; surrounding spaces are removed and control characters are refused.

fields.name: Versions
fields.meaning: Distinguish the version in effect from a draft awaiting approval.
fields.values: Version numbers, or no version in effect / no draft.
fields.rules: Read-only; a record can have a current version and a draft at the same time.

actions.name: Add specimen type
actions.does: Register the code and name, then open the record.
actions.availableWhen: Manage configuration; code is not already used.
actions.result: Creates the named record. Draft and approve its content separately.

actions.name: Open row
actions.does: Show the selected record and its versions.
actions.result: The record page opens. Click its row or press Enter.

actions.name: Clear find / Clear filters
actions.does: Remove the selected search or filter constraints.
actions.availableWhen: A search or filter is applied.
actions.result: The list expands; no saved configuration changes.

restrictions: Adding a name and code alone does not create an approved definition.
workflow: Search before adding a record to avoid duplicates.
Open the existing record or add the laboratory-approved code and name.
Review its version state before changing it.

troubleshooting.recovery: Clear find and filters; if the record is still absent, ask the configuration owner before adding a new code.

pages.title: Specimen type validity policy
pages.purpose: Define the laboratory-approved categories and required consequences of specimen-validity assessment.
pages.access: View with the configuration access offered to your account. Adding and drafting require Manage configuration; approval and retirement require Approve configuration. The engine checks authority again when saving.

fields.name: Version, Status and Versions list
fields.meaning: Identify exactly which definition you are viewing and whether it can govern new work.
fields.values: Draft; Approved; Replaced; Retired. Version numbers increase within the record.
fields.rules: Read-only. On opening, the draft is preferred, then the version in effect, then the newest. Choose a version explicitly before review.

fields.name: Drafted, Approved by, Effective, Retired and Retirement reason
fields.meaning: Show who authored and authorized the definition, when it applied and why it ended.
fields.values: Recorded people, laboratory-local times, effective period and reason; Not approved or Not yet effective when applicable.
fields.rules: Read-only. Replacement ends the earlier effective period without deleting its content.

fields.name: Reason (Retire version)
fields.meaning: Explain why this approved version must stop being used for new work.
fields.values: Specific laboratory explanation, up to 1,000 characters.
fields.rules: Required for retirement; retained in history.

fields.name: Self-approval confirmation
fields.meaning: Explicitly records that the draft author is also approving it without another reviewer.
fields.values: An initially unchecked confirmation, shown when the engine requires it.
fields.rules: Available only if laboratory policy permits this duty to be performed by one person. Closing the dialog clears this confirmation.

fields.name: Code (each Categories row)
fields.meaning: Stable laboratory identifier for a validity category.
fields.values: Letters, digits, period, underscore or hyphen; up to 64 characters.
fields.rules: Required; unique within the policy version.

fields.name: Label
fields.meaning: Name of the validity category shown to staff.
fields.rules: Required. No clinical categories are preselected.

fields.name: Action
fields.meaning: Consequence associated with this validity category.
fields.values: No action; Report with a qualifier; Hold the results; Request recollection; Add a comment.
fields.rules: Required; choose according to approved laboratory policy, not a value suggested by this guide.

fields.name: Qualifier text
fields.meaning: Exact report wording for a category that reports with a qualifier.
fields.rules: Shown and required only for Report with a qualifier. Other actions save no qualifier text.

actions.name: Choose Version / Previous / Next
actions.does: Inspect a particular saved definition or move through the records from the directory.
actions.availableWhen: A version or neighboring record exists.
actions.result: The selected content and its history appear; no definition changes.

actions.name: New draft version / New draft from this version
actions.does: Start an empty definition or copy the selected definition for revision.
actions.availableWhen: Manage configuration and no open draft for this record.
actions.result: A form opens. Saving creates the next draft; it is not yet in effect.

actions.name: Open draft version / Edit draft
actions.does: Return to the open proposal and revise its content.
actions.availableWhen: A draft exists; editing requires Manage configuration and the draft author.
actions.result: Save draft updates the draft revision; approved versions remain immutable.

actions.name: Approve version
actions.does: Confirm the reviewed draft and make it current.
actions.availableWhen: Approve configuration, current draft revision, valid dependencies, and the applicable separation-of-duties rule.
actions.result: Approved content becomes immutable immediately; the previous current version becomes Replaced.

actions.name: Retire version
actions.does: End use of an approved version for new work while retaining its history.
actions.availableWhen: Approve configuration, an approved version and a reason; dependency checks must pass.
actions.result: The version is retained as Retired. Existing work keeps the version it used.

actions.name: Save draft / Cancel
actions.does: Submit the draft form, or close it without saving.
actions.availableWhen: Required fields are supplied for Save draft.
actions.result: A successful save opens the saved draft; a refusal leaves the form available for correction.

actions.name: Add category / Remove category
actions.does: Adjust the categories in the draft policy.
actions.availableWhen: While creating or editing the draft.
actions.result: At least one category must remain when saving; the complete list is reviewed together.

restrictions: Only one draft may be open per record, and only its author may edit it. Saving a draft is separate from approval.
A stale revision is refused. Reload and review the current version before repeating an edit or approval.
Laboratory approval establishes the configured definition; this software does not supply clinical validation or assay acceptance criteria.
Policy categories do not calculate or establish clinical validity by themselves. The responsible laboratory supplies their meaning and intended use.
workflow: Open the specimen type and select its policy version.
Create or edit a draft with each authorized category, label and action.
Enter exact qualifier wording only where that action applies.
Save, review and approve the policy before expecting it to be current.

troubleshooting.recovery: Arrange another authorized reviewer unless laboratory policy expressly permits self-approval; if permitted, read and explicitly confirm the prompt.

troubleshooting.problem: Revision conflict or an existing draft
troubleshooting.recovery: Open the current record and draft, compare its content with your intended change, then retry only the applicable action.

troubleshooting.problem: A receiving workflow lacks the expected category
troubleshooting.recovery: Check the specimen type and its policy version in effect. Saving an unapproved draft alone does not update active choices.
